turns.text: Itch first. Behind the left ear, under the fur, where the patch went in — not a bite, not a bug, a frequency with legs, needling deeper the longer it's ignored. Paw comes up to scratch and stops halfway, the itch resolving mid-motion into a taste instead: burnt copper, three streets before any copper's actually close.

the relay gantry runs cable-strung between two arcology spires, thirty stories up, laundry lines gone slack with rain sagging alongside the transmission masts like nobody's told anyone which lines still carry washing and which carry someone's phone call. wind cuts sideways through the lattice, driving the masts' hum down into the metal underfoot — five frequencies stacked at once, none of them agreeing, all of them looking for the same ear.

Five frequencies stacked wrong is worse than one loud one — worse because it doesn't sound like sound at all, comes through more like a smear of color low across the same five feet of catwalk, mustard-bright where a mast's beam crosses, gone violet where it doesn't. Tongue works the air once, chasing a taste none of this is actually supposed to have.

the nearest mast leans a few degrees off true, service ladder rusted to the housing, a NEKOCORP decal half stripped where somebody's picked at the sticker with their teeth before — not tonight, weeks old, edges long since curled dry. below the gantry, three stories down, a night market stall throws light and grease-smoke up between the buildings, and pressed flat against its awning post, unmoving, a shape holds still with both eyes wide open, reflecting the stall's sign on a loop, blink never arriving.

.-=====-.
     ( [0]  .. )
      '-==Y==-'
       |  |  |
   ...picking through the neon rain...

POPUP doesn't need those eyes explained twice — seen that stillness before, the kind that isn't sleep and isn't watching either, just stuck open. Not this catwalk's business. Attention goes back to the mast's decal, teeth finding the same worried edge some other mouth left, working it a little further loose out of nothing but habit.

the decal peels back further than expected, corner tearing clean to reveal a service panel underneath, cover cracked and hanging on one hinge. inside: a nest of cable, warm, six or seven strands humming at once, one stripped raw where teeth or claws or both got there first. static bleeds faint off the exposed copper, and for anyone whose senses do this backward, the static tastes like a color too — gray, mostly, streaked with something that flares gold every few seconds on its own private clock.

Gray-with-gold-flares is at least a taste worth finishing, which is more than tonight's given so far. Tongue finds the stripped strand, close, not touching, close enough anyway for the gold-flare to spike into something sharper — a half-second of pure copper flavor, then a ringing that isn't in the ears at all but somewhere behind the eyes instead.

the ringing has a source, eventually — three masts over, a signal drone rides the wind on fixed wings instead of rotors, silent except for the cut of air over its ailerons, banking slow along the gantry's line on a patrol that doesn't officially exist. it isn't hunting. it's counting — antenna to antenna, checking which ones are still broadcasting on schedule and which have gone quiet since the last pass.

Counting isn't hunting, but a body doesn't always trust the difference in time — weight drops flat against the walkway grating, ears pinned, the gold-flare taste souring fast into something closer to fear-flavor, sharp and metallic same as the copper but wrong now, unwanted.

the drone's wingtip camera sweeps the mast row without slowing for the gantry itself, logging antenna status the way it logs it every night this stretch has stood — one flagged silent three towers back, nothing here worth the extra half-second. it banks off east, wing-cut fading under the masts' five-note hum until it's gone entirely.

Fear-flavor doesn't fade as fast as the drone does — lingers a while after, souring the copper-taste underneath it, until enough of tonight's ordinary hum crowds back in to argue it down to nothing. Body stays flat a count longer than it needs to, old habit outlasting the actual danger.

rain thickens for a few minutes then thins again, same as it's done all night, beading along the slack laundry lines and dripping in three different rhythms depending which line it's found. the market stall below cycles its awning light through one more loop, POPUP's reflection blinking on the fabric though the eyes themselves still don't, and somewhere past both, a distant broadcast — corporate, clipped, half-swallowed by the wind — chews through someone else's name and someone else's bounty before the wind takes the rest of it.

Someone else's bounty is someone else's night. Attention narrows back down to what's actually underpaw — cold grating, cooling copper-taste, hunger finally loud enough now to out-argue the leftover fear. Nose drops, working the walkway's seams for whatever the rain hasn't washed off yet.

the seams give up a scrap worth following — grease residue tracked up from the market stall on somebody's boot tread hours ago, faint but real, leading three panels down toward a maintenance ladder bolted where the gantry meets the second spire. the ladder's rungs are slick, but the smell gets stronger with every one.

Grease-trail wins outright this time, nothing left to argue it down. Climb starts careful anyway, rain-slick rungs taken one at a time, claws doing more work than paws, the mast-hum fading rung by rung into something almost like quiet the lower the ladder goes.

the ladder ends at a narrow service landing tucked behind the spire's cladding, out of the wind entirely, and there — wedged where the grease-trail runs out — a dropped food-cart wrapper, licked at already by rain but not by anything with a mouth. the quiet down here holds different than the gantry's did: no mast-hum, no static, just water finding gutters and, faint under that, the market's grease-smoke settling instead of rising.

Quiet without the five-note argument overhead is its own kind of relief, worth almost as much as what's actually in the wrapper. Jaw works fast at what's left, the last of the gold-flare taste fading out entirely now, replaced by something plainer, easier, just food.

nothing follows up the ladder. the landing holds its stolen quiet, wrapper licked clean and left where it fell, rain finding the same three gutters it's found every night this spire has stood. up on the gantry, the masts keep their five frequencies stacked and disagreeing, patient, and POPUP's eyes keep not blinking at a sign that isn't even lit anymore, waiting on nothing in particular.

Settle down against the landing's dry corner, tail wrapped tight, one ear still cocked toward the ladder out of habit though nothing's climbed it. The itch behind the ear finally reads as just an itch again, ordinary, no color attached, no taste left riding under it.

the spire holds its temperature through the last of the rain, indifferent, the grease-trail gone cold and unremarkable now that it's been followed to its end. dawn is hours off. somewhere above, the flagged-silent mast three towers back stays silent, uncounted again until the drone's next pass, and the gantry keeps its rhythm of hum and static and dripping water going without anyone left awake to mind it.
